Ohalo Genetics is an American agricultural biotechnology company founded in 2019 and led by CEO David Friedberg, developing plant-breeding platforms and proprietary crop varieties.
Its flagship Boosted Breeding technology — marketed as "2x + 2x = 4x" — alters the reproductive circuitry of parent plants so each parent passes its entire genome to the next generation rather than a random half, producing polyploid offspring that carry the full genetic contribution of both parents and, in early field trials, substantially higher yields.
Ohalo pairs this with an Agile Breeding service and a True Seed program that ships uniform, disease-free seedlings directly to growers, with active programs in potato, almond (the FruitionOne self-fertile Nonpareil variety), strawberry and corn, delivered through partnerships such as the Allied Potato partnership and a strawberry consortium.
The company sells plant genetics and breeding services to agricultural partners; it is not a software vendor and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.
Ohalo Genetics is profiled on the APIs.io network.

Ohalo (Ohalo Genetics) is a California-based plant breeding and agricultural genetics company that develops novel breeding systems and improved crop varieties intended to raise yield, resiliency and genetic diversity while using fewer natural resources.
Its core technology, marketed as Boosted Breeding, uses proteins and gene-editing techniques to switch off the reproductive mechanism that normally splits parental genes during meiosis, so that gametes are clonal and offspring inherit the complete genome of both parents rather than a random half from each.
The company describes the resulting polyploid "Boosted" plants as having more beneficial trait combinations, improved heterozygosity, and yield gains it claims can reach 50-100%+, along with the ability to stack traits and produce genetically uniform "true seed" in crops that are normally propagated vegetatively.
Ohalo Genetics offers Boosted Breeding and Agile Breeding services across crops including potatoes, corn, almonds and berries, and markets a True Seed service delivering uniform, disease-free seedlings to growers.
Its product areas are organized around potato, almond and strawberry, plus other crops.
...
In almonds it announced FruitionOne, described as the first self-fertile Nonpareil almond variety, and it has organized an Ohalo Strawberry Consortium to develop strawberries delivered as true seed.
The company states its plants are not transgenic and do not introduce non-native DNA.
...
Recent announcements include a strategic partnership with Allied Potato covering the global potato industry, the launch of the Ohalo Strawberry Consortium to develop more flavorful strawberries sold as true seed, a joint effort with UF/IFAS and the Florida strawberry industry against a fungal disease, the FruitionOne self-fertile Nonpareil almond variety, and the appointments of Justin Wolfe as president and chief operating officer and Rob Dunlop as VP, global commercial.
...
Boosted Breeding relies on several novel proteins and techniques that turn off the reproductive circuits responsible for halving parental genomes, causing gametes formed through meiosis to instead be clonal and proceed through mitosis, preserving the full maternal and paternal genomes.

hits.title: New GMO Alert: Strawberry Shortcut — What the Biotech Industry ...
hits.snippet:
Self-Claimed “Non-GMO” vs. Non-GMO Project Verified: Why EVYLO Chose Independent Verification
- **Several biotech companies are developing gene-edited strawberries** engineered for durability, longer shelf life and improved flavor.
None have reached the commercial food supply.
...
We’re monitoring several GMO strawberry developments, and while none have reached your grocery store yet, what’s happening in the lab and greenhouse is worth understanding now.
...
These developments are listed in order of announcement, spanning a product already on the market to university-level research that has yet to be monetized.
...
In 2021, J.R. Simplot Company and Plant Science Inc.
joined forces with the goal of bringing the first genetically modified strawberry to market, using CRISPR to extend strawberries’ growing season, reduce waste and improve shelf life.
...
As of this writing, no product has reached market and the companies have not issued public updates on their timeline.
- In 2024, Dutch biotech company Hudson River Biotechnology announced the successful regeneration of a strawberry plant from a single gene-edited cell using their proprietary TiGER workflow.
The company says TiGER allows developers to edit genes without introducing foreign DNA and ensures that edits are expressed consistently throughout the plant.
The workflow is reportedly being used to develop strawberries with resistance to fungal infection, a common and costly cause of crop loss.
...
Earlier this year, researchers from the University of Florida, Kongju National University, Chungbuk National University and the National Institute of Horticultural and Herbal Science of Korea announced the development of a white-fleshed strawberry.
The team used CRISPR to knock out the color-producing gene in the commercially grown “Florida Brilliance” cultivar.
It’s unclear whether this work could lead to a commercially-available GMO white-fleshed strawberry in the future, or if the exploration of gene editing in polyploidal crops could be developed to impact other traits.
...
- Biotech company Ohalo is taking a different approach by intervening in how strawberries are propagated.
Conventional propagation depends on runners because breeding from seed is unpredictable with such a complex genome.
Ohalo’s “Boosted Breeding” system suppresses the mechanism that normally delivers only half the genes from each parent, so offspring inherit the complete genome from both parents.
The company says the boosted seed produces uniform seed that could replace runner propagation.
In 2025, Ohalo formed the Ohalo Strawberry Consortium with California strawberry producers, with the stated goal of bringing “consumer-preferred, more flavorful strawberries” to market.
...
Because the only strawberry in the global supply chain engineered for commercial use is processed into a powder to treat gingivitis in dogs and cats, we feel confident you aren’t going to encounter one at your local grocery store, farm stand, or u-pick anytime soon.
Our researchers will keep you posted if that changes.
...
Ohalo is describing its gene-edited strawberry seed as non-GMO.
That characterization conflicts with the internationally accepted definition of a living modified organism established under the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety — the same definition on which the Non-GMO Project Standard‘s definition of GMO is based.
...
**Are there GMO strawberries at the grocery store?**
Not yet.
As of publication, no genetically engineered strawberries have entered the commercial food supply.
The only GMO strawberry currently on the market is a veterinary pharmaceutical sold in Japan.
